slides.title: A map that fits in a pocket
slides.text: Tally unrolls a map of the village. On the paper the mill is 6 centimeters from the gate, but nobody walks in centimeters. The scale in the corner says how far each centimeter really is.

slides.title: Every centimeter is 250 meters
slides.text: A scale of 1 cm : 250 m means each centimeter on the map stands for 250 meters on the ground. The mill is 6 centimeters away, so the walk is 6 × 250 = 1500 meters. To go from the ground to the map, divide by 250.

visual.label: Centimeters on the map and meters on the ground

slides.title: The scale as an equation
slides.text: Let c be centimeters on the map and d be meters on the ground. Then d = 250c, and 250 is the constant of proportionality. On a graph, the point (1, 250) shows the scale, and (0, 0) says that no map distance is no ground distance.

slides.title: Area: both sides are scaled
slides.text: A field is 3 cm by 2 cm on a plan at 1 cm : 10 m. Its real sides are 30 m and 20 m, so its real area is 30 × 20 = 600 square meters. Each square centimeter of paper stands for 10 × 10 = 100 square meters, not 10.

visual.label: A field plan, 3 centimeters by 2 centimeters

focus.cue: The long side: 3 cm on paper is 30 m.
The short side: 2 cm on paper is 20 m.
Six paper squares, each 100 square meters.

slides.title: A new scale, the same wall
slides.text: A wall is 6 cm long on a plan at 1 cm : 4 m, so it is really 24 meters. On a new plan at 1 cm : 8 m, each centimeter holds more ground, so the drawing is shorter: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 cm. Find the real length first.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for maps and plans.

words.means: how far on the ground one unit on the map stands for
a drawing with every length in the same ratio to the real thing
the real length on the ground, not the length on the paper
a rule written with an equals sign, such as d = 250c

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Scale Scout at Map and Ground. Use the scale to plan a walk, put a pin on the map, find a real area and redraw a wall. Run each plan and see where it lands.
slides.alt: Scale Scout on a phone: a map with a road from the gate to the mill over a ruler in centimeters, the scale 1 cm to 250 m, and a stepper for the meters.
